subject: Data isolation follow-up — Dedicated vs Private VPC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@finsecure.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Data isolation follow-up — Dedicated vs Private VPC

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so we’re all aligned:

Summary of your requirements (as I heard them):
- FinSecure will be processing regulated financial data and needs strict data isolation; no customer data may be accessible outside your VPC/account without explicit control.
- You prefer customer-managed keys (ideally HSM-backed) for encryption-at-rest and in-transit.
- Audit logging and evidence of no egress are required for vendor assessments (SOC2 + internal audit).
- Timeline: target decision & POC in ~8–12 weeks; budget TBD.

Deployment options we discussed:
1) Hosted API — fastest but does not meet your no-egress requirement for raw data (not recommended here).
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — we can provision isolated GPU pools; with network-level constructs (VPC peering, PrivateLink, customer-managed encryption) we can significantly restrict egress, but it still uses Redwood-managed control plane and our runtime.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — full customer-managed deployment: control plane in your VPC (or on-prem), model weights and runtime run in your environment, Redwood provides the deployment package and integrations.

Open/clarifying questions for your team:
1) Are there any vendor personnel that will need interactive access to instances, even under jump-host controls?
2) Which KMS provider do you prefer (AWS KMS, CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault) and is attested HSM required?
3) Do you require model weights to be brought on-prem (air-gapped) or can they reside in customer cloud storage within your account?
4) For audit logs, is forwarding to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/Log Analytics) acceptable, and what retention window do you need?

Attachments: I’ve attached a short one-pager comparing Dedicated vs Private VPC for reference.

Next steps I propose:
- Dev deep-dive: schedule a 60-minute technical call with Dev and your infra/security team (Dev Patel to join) — proposed 6/8 or 6/9.
- Share your security questionnaire so we can start filling it out.
- Preliminary pricing: we’ll send an estimated pricing sheet for Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private deployment setup + monthly run-rate.

Can you please confirm availability for the technical call and attach the security questionnaire?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Redwood_Dedicated_vs_Private_VPC_one_pager.pdf (brief comparison PDF)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few points and adding our constraints:
- We process regulated financial transaction data and certain datasets qualify as restricted (cannot leave our VPC/account).
- We require customer-managed keys and prefer HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM or Azure Dedicated HSM).
- No vendor-managed control-plane access to raw logs or data is acceptable without our explicit approval and audit controls.
- Audit evidence: we need demonstrable proof of no egress and logs that show all network calls; retention requirement is 7 years for audit purposes.

Attached is our security questionnaire — please have your security/engineering team complete sections on network topology, key management, and logging.

Regarding deployment preference: Private VPC/on-prem is our preferred path if it meets your feature requirements (model updates, monitoring, and support). Dedicated could be considered if you can show the following in writing:
1) Network architecture demonstrating no egress outside our VPC/account.
2) KMS integration details and proof that keys are fully customer-controlled and not exfiltrated.
3) Logging/audit integration points and sample logs.

We can do a technical deep-dive next week. My team’s availability: 6/8 (10–12 ET) or 6/9 (13–15 ET).

Thanks,
Alicia Ramos
Director of Security, FinSecure
alicia.ramos@finsecure.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Data isolation follow-up — Dedicated vs Private VPC

Hi Alicia, Marissa —

Appreciate the detailed constraints. A few technical clarifications that should help your security team evaluate options:

Dedicated (Reserved capacity)
- Network: We can deploy Dedicated GPU pools in a customer-dedicated subnet and establish VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink so all ingress/egress is between your VPC and the dedicated subnet. No public internet egress is required; NAT/firewall rules can be locked down.
- Data residency: Customer data (request payloads, KV cache) can be configured to never persist to shared storage; ephemeral storage lives on the instance and is wiped on termination. We can also mount customer-owned EBS-backed volumes in your account for any persisted artifacts.
- KMS: Supports AWS KMS and CloudHSM; we can integrate customer-managed keys and never export key material from the managed HSM. For Azure/AWS/GCP we support their KMS offerings and HSM import where available.
- Control plane: By default the Redwood control plane coordinates deployments; for Dedicated we offer a 'control-plane-lite' configuration that minimizes metadata flow and can be configured over PrivateLink to your VPC.

Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Full customer control: Runtime, model weights, and storage run inside your network. Redwood provides an appliance/deployment bundle; you control access, updates, and key management entirely.
- HSM & air-gap: We support HSM-backed keys and can provide an on-prem deployment that is air-gapped; model weights can be delivered via secure transfer and stored in customer-only storage.
- Audit/logging: We support forwarding all runtime logs to your SIEM (CloudWatch, Splunk, or S3) and can provide signed attestations for key operations.

Other notes:
- KV cache & inference internals: The runtime keeps KV cache in local memory; it is not written to disk unless explicitly configured. We can disable telemetry that contains prompt contents.
- E2E encryption: TLS between clients and runtime + customer-managed KMS for at-rest encryption. We can provide sample network diagrams and a minimal config for a no-egress Dedicated topology.

Attachments: redwood_private_network_diagram_v1.png (network diagram), security_design_notes.txt (high-level answers to your questionnaire sections 2-4).

I’m happy to run the technical deep-dive and demo our no-egress topology. Proposed slots (per Alicia): 6/8 10:30 ET or 6/9 13:30 ET — I can do both.

Action items for us:
- I’ll upload the network diagram and notes to the ticket and provide a short summarized answer to the questionnaire by EOD 6/6.
- Marissa: I’ll need the official questionnaire file and any specific sections the audit team prioritizes.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
